craft_notes: Sthāyin: wonder at the coiled one (kuṇḍalinī unnamed — never named in L4 either). Sanskrit first: locus (mid-wheel), nature (unstruck), stripes (lines), coil (serpent) → L4 sets locus+nature line 1, stripes+coil line 2. Rows: row 2 (the serpent kept whole line 2 — never split, the coil IS the image). Rupture: comma-dash after 'ray' — vision narrowed to the coil. Close: end-weight on posture ('she lay' — coiled rest). Minimal pass: 'slender ray' for kalā (digit-as-ray, singable; doctrine kept in cite). Read aloud: line 1 stands (mid-wheel, ray), line 2 coils down (above, below, lay). Rejected: naming her kuṇḍalinī — killed: Sanskrit withholds the name, song must too; 'sleeping' for coiled — killed: kuṭilā is coiled shape, sleep is imported state.

lines: Mid-wheel she stands, the Unstruck's slender ray,
ringed above, below — serpent-coiled she lay.
l4.sanskrit_cite: kandacakrasya madhyasthā tv anāhatamayī kalā / adhaūrdhve rekhāsaṃyuktā bhujaṃgakuṭilākṛtiḥ

reads_against.argmap: The sign is the unstruck digit seen serpent-coiled in the bulb-wheel.
c1_essence: The unstruck digit mid-wheel, line-bound, serpent-coiled — the sign.
reads_against.c1_rasa: adbhuta with vīra-utsāha (wonder braced by resolve)
